about: Every tag in a note's text, in order: its frontmatter tags, then the #tags in its body (fenced code and inline code skipped). Duplicates are kept.

cases.name: at line start and after a list marker
trailing slashes dropped
cases.note: Unverified in Obsidian.

cases.name: digits only is not a tag
needs a space or line start before the #
cases.note: Obsidian likely agrees for a#b and \#f; (#e) unverified.

cases.name: a URL fragment is not a tag
a wikilink heading is not a tag
combining accent (decomposed é)
cases.note: TS stops at U+0301 (a mark, not \p{L}). Obsidian's tag pattern is believed to exclude only whitespace, ASCII punctuation and U+2000-206F / U+2E00-2E7F, so it keeps the mark. Verify.

cases.name: Devanagari vowel signs
cases.note: TS stops at the first vowel sign (Mc/Mn, not \p{L}). Obsidian likely keeps the word whole (see the combining accent case). Verify.

cases.name: emoji
cases.note: TS allows only letters, digits, _ - /. Obsidian likely allows emoji in tags. Verify.

cases.name: CJK full stop
cases.note: U+3002 is outside the ranges Obsidian is believed to exclude. Verify.

cases.name: double-backtick inline code
cases.note: TS blanks single-backtick pairs only (`[^`]*`), so it splits the span at the inner backtick. CommonMark (and so Obsidian, likely) reads ``#a ` #b`` as one code span. Rust's blank_inline_code (links) does it the CommonMark way.

cases.name: a shorter fence does not close a longer one
the other marker does not close a fence
fence indented with a tab is not a fence
cases.note: TS: a fence opens with at most 3 spaces, so a tab-indented ``` is not one. CommonMark agrees (a tab is 4 columns: an indented code line). Rust's fence_open trims any whitespace up to 3 characters, so it opens a fence here (see links.json).

cases.name: fence indented 4 spaces is not a fence
closing fence indented 4 spaces does not close
cases.note: TS and CommonMark: a closing fence has at most 3 spaces of indent, so the block runs on to the end. Rust's fence_close trims any indent and closes here (see links.json).

cases.name: closing fence with text after it does not close
a backtick in a backtick fence's info string: not a fence
unclosed fence runs to the end
indented code block
cases.note: TS has no indented-code-block rule. Obsidian probably does not tag inside an indented code block. Unverified; no obsidian value given.

cases.name: frontmatter YAML comment after the value
frontmatter key in any case
cases.note: Unverified in Obsidian.

cases.name: frontmatter must start on line 1
cases.note: Frontmatter must start on line 1; here it does not, so the --- block is body text.

cases.name: a # inside frontmatter is not a body tag
BOM before frontmatter
cases.note: TS: frontmatter must start with ---, and a BOM comes first. Rust's parse_note strips a BOM. Obsidian likely reads the frontmatter. Verify.

cases.name: nested tag four deep
cases.note: Obsidian nested tags are slash-separated to any depth. Same list.

cases.name: digits with a slash are a tag
cases.note: A slash is a non-numerical character, so this is a tag even though each side is digits. #1984 alone is not. Obsidian agrees.

cases.name: digits with a hyphen or underscore are a tag
cases.note: Hyphen and underscore count as the required non-numerical character. Obsidian agrees.

cases.name: a dot or comma after digits is not a tag
cases.note: The punctuation ends the token and the rest is only digits, so nothing is kept. Obsidian does not treat #12.34 as a tag either.

cases.name: trailing punctuation ends a tag
cases.note: ?, :, ; and . are not tag characters. (#spaced) has no space before the #, so it is not a tag. Obsidian agrees.

cases.name: an apostrophe or quote ends a tag
cases.note: The apostrophe and the quote are not tag characters. Obsidian agrees.

cases.name: a fullwidth hash is not a tag
cases.note: Only ASCII # starts a tag. Obsidian agrees.

cases.name: a tag in link text, not in the URL
cases.note: The # in the link text follows a space, so it is a tag. The # in each URL does not. Obsidian agrees.

cases.name: a space before a fragment makes it a tag
cases.note: The existing URL case has no space. With a space, the # starts a tag. Obsidian agrees.

cases.name: a heading line can still hold a tag
cases.note: The heading hashes are not a tag. #release/1 is; the dot ends it. Obsidian allows the same characters.

cases.name: a numeric hash in a heading is not a tag
cases.note: #123 is only digits. Obsidian agrees.

cases.name: a tag in a blockquote or a table cell
cases.note: Both are ordinary text. Obsidian indexes them.

cases.name: a tag inside an HTML comment
cases.note: TS has no comment rule. Obsidian does not index a tag inside <!-- -->.

cases.name: a tag inside a %% comment
cases.note: Obsidian hides %% comments and does not index tags inside them. TS has no comment rule.

cases.name: frontmatter string and legacy tag key
cases.note: A plain string is one tag, and the legacy tag: key counts too. Obsidian accepts both.

cases.name: frontmatter list drops numeric and dotted values
cases.note: 1984 is only digits. 12.34 has a dot, so the whole value is rejected rather than cut to 12. Obsidian rejects both.

cases.name: frontmatter emoji tag
cases.note: Obsidian's tag format includes emoji. A frontmatter value must match the whole token, and TS allows only letters, digits, _, - and /, so the emoji is dropped. The body case is the existing emoji case.

cases.name: frontmatter combining accent
cases.note: A body tag keeps the letters before the mark. A frontmatter value has to match the whole token, so TS drops it. Obsidian is believed to keep the mark, as in the body case. Verify.

cases.name: frontmatter aliases are not tags
cases.note: aliases is a different property. Obsidian agrees.

cases.name: frontmatter quoted hash and a numeric tag
cases.note: A leading # is stripped. #1984 is still only digits. Obsidian strips the hash and rejects the numeric value.

cases.name: frontmatter comma string
cases.note: Comma-separated string form. 1984 is dropped. Precomposed é is a letter. Obsidian agrees.

cases.name: letters from Arabic and Japanese, nested
cases.note: Alphabetical letters from other scripts are allowed, including inside a nested tag. Obsidian agrees.

cases.name: a hash glued to an emoji is not a tag
cases.note: The # has to follow a space or the start of the line. Obsidian uses the same boundary.

cases.name: a hash on a fence's info string is not a tag
cases.note: The fence line is not scanned, and the inside of the block is skipped. Obsidian agrees.

cases.name: empty slash segments
cases.note: TS keeps an empty segment and a leading slash. Unverified in Obsidian, so no obsidian value.

cases.name: three casings of one tag
cases.note: This list keeps each spelling. Obsidian's tag index treats them as one tag and displays the casing it saw first. Each occurrence is still a tag, so the list is not given an obsidian override.
